name: Addon Repository: `accelerated` publish mode alongside `hotfix`
description:
## Why?

Kateřina Stanislava Dvořáková (partner program) asks for a second "publish straight to production" mode next to `hotfix`, working name `accelerated`. It must behave **exactly** like `hotfix` — the update goes live without the standard review round — but cover a different case: planned **updates in an accelerated regime**, not incident fixes. Those updates then have to be unambiguously distinguishable from real hotfixes **for analytics**.

Today they cannot be told apart, because `hotfix` is not a deploy mode at all — it is only a commit-message keyword:

- `getCommitType()` (`src/commits.ts`) matches `hotfix` / `merge` in the head-commit message of an **unauthorised** push to the default branch. The only thing it drives is which title/body the app uses for the GitHub issue it opens (`branchProtect.commitTypes.hotfix` in `src/config.json`).
- The production publish is triggered **independently** of that: any push to `main`/`master` starts `assets/shoptetAddon.workflow.yml`, and `handleWorkflowRun()` then uploads the artifact over SFTP and sends the custom-codes call via `updateCustomCodes()`.
- That payload (`CustomCodes`: `repoName`, `sha`, `scripts`, `styles`, `markups`) carries **no** mode information. Nothing downstream can tell a hotfix publish from a regular one — so there is currently not even a baseline to compare an accelerated publish against.

Consequence for scoping: this is a **labelling and telemetry change**, not a new deployment pipeline. The deploy behaviour Kateřina describes ("same as hotfix") already exists for free — the work is in marking the publish so it can be told apart.

## What?

**1 — **`accelerated` commit type

Add `Accelerated: 'accelerated'` to the `CommitType` map in `src/commits.ts` and a matching `branchProtect.commitTypes.accelerated` entry (title/body) in `src/config.json`, so an accelerated push to the default branch gets its own GitHub issue instead of the 🔥 hotfix one.

Two things need a decision, not just code (see Open questions): `getCommitType()` uses a naive `commitMessage.toLowerCase().includes(type)` over `Object.values(CommitType)` in declaration order, so the match is **not** prefix-anchored (unlike what the partner docs promise) and **first declared type wins** if a message contains two keywords.

**2 — carry the mode in the custom-codes payload**

Extend `CustomCodes` (`src/shoptetApiEndpoints.ts`) with an explicit mode field, e.g. `updateMode: 'standard' | 'hotfix' | 'accelerated'`, and set it in `handleWorkflowRun()`.

Note the handler boundary: the mode is detectable on the `push` event, but the payload is assembled on `workflow_run.completed` — a different handler with no shared state. The mode therefore has to be re-derived in `handleWorkflowRun()` from the run's head commit (`workflow_run.head_commit.message`, or an `octokit.repos.getCommit()` on `head_sha`), which also covers manual `workflow_dispatch` re-runs. This is the one part of the change that can grow beyond its estimate.

**3 — Tests and partner docs**

`test/commits.test.ts` + a `test/fixtures/push.accelerated.json` fixture alongside the existing hotfix one; a new section in `docs/docs/tutorial-basics/recommended-flows.md` (next to "I have an approved add-on, but I need to hotfix") and a mention in `docs/docs/intro.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A push to the default branch with the accelerated keyword is recognised as its own commit type and opens its own GitHub issue (not the hotfix one), with the existing label protection intact
- [ ] Keyword matching is documented and deterministic: agreed syntax, agreed precedence when a message contains more than one keyword, covered by tests
- [ ] The custom-codes payload carries an explicit mode for **all three** cases — standard, hotfix, accelerated — including on manual `workflow_dispatch` runs
- [ ] `yarn test` and `yarn lint` pass; new fixture + tests cover accelerated, hotfix and standard pushes
- [ ] Write documentation describes the accelerated flow for the Partner

## Open questions

1. Final keyword and syntax — `Accelerated: ` prefix? Anchored to the start of the commit message (as the docs promise for `Hotfix: `) or matched anywhere (as the code does today)?
2. Precedence when a commit message contains both keywords.
3. Should an accelerated push still open a "please describe the reason" issue, or a lighter informational one without the hotfix alarm tone?
4. Does the mode need to appear only in the custom-codes payload, or also on the GitHub deployment (`createDeployment()` currently hardcodes `environment: 'Production'`) and/or on the issue labels?
5. Is `accelerated` the final name, given it will be partner-facing in commit messages and docs?
